Subject to the completion of certain conditions, including regulatory approval, as a result of the transaction with Ligado, we expect our network will be enhanced by our long-term access to up to 45 MHz of the lower mid-band satellite spectrum in the United States (“U.S.”) and Canada through our usage agreements.
We expect the acquisition will further enhance our network by up to 60 MHz of mid-band satellite spectrum globally.
We intend to work with MNOs to offer the SpaceMobile Service to the MNOs’ end-user customers.
We intend to seek to use a revenue-sharing business model for the SpaceMobile Service in our agreements with MNOs.
As a result of the incremental coverage created by the planned SpaceMobile Service, we believe that MNOs will have the opportunity to increase subscribers’ average revenue per user.

We also intend to leverage our patented technology, including the large phased array and high power capability of our BB satellites, for a variety of non-communication and communication applications in the government sector.

In connection with the loss of BB7, we have received insurance recovery with respect to a portion of the total loss associated with this event and expect a replacement launch pursuant to the terms of the applicable contract with the launch provider.

We believe the larger aperture array will provide greater spectrum reuse, enhanced signal strength and increased capacity, thereby reducing the necessary number of satellites to achieve service coverage as compared to smaller apertures.

In addition, when we introduce our own AST5000 ASIC chip in the Block 2 BB satellites, we expect to achieve materially greater throughput capacity of up to 40 MHz per beam and up to 10,000 MHz of processing bandwidth per Block 2 BB satellite, require less power and offer a lower overall unit cost.
In parallel to assembly, integration and testing of Block 2 BB satellites based on our ASIC chip, we expect to continue to assemble and launch Block 2 BB satellites based on FPGA chips.

In addition to our currently contracted 10 launches, our expected new launches based on our Defense Priorities and Allocations System (“DPAS”) rating and our newly signed non-binding agreement for at least five (5) additional launches, we now expect to have launches to support a total of over 100 BB satellites on a cumulative basis by the end of 2028.

We have commenced our launch campaign with the launch of BB6 on December 23, 2025 and based on our current expectations regarding launch availability, we are targeting approximately 45 BB satellites by the middle of 2027.

We are developing a phased satellite deployment plan and a corresponding commercial launch plan of the SpaceMobile Service based on targeted geographical markets to provide the SpaceMobile Service to the most commercially attractive MNO markets.

We expect that such a successful commercial service would enable us to attract additional capital to continue to assemble and launch additional BB satellites to expand our capacity and geographic coverage area, although there can be no assurance that such capital would be available on terms acceptable to us, or at all.

We plan to achieve noncontinuous SpaceMobile Service in the selected, targeted geographical markets with the launch and operation of a total of 25 BB satellites (five Block 1 BB satellites and 20 Block 2 BB satellites).

We believe we can enable Continuous SpaceMobile Service coverage across key markets such as the United States, Europe, Japan and other strategic markets with the launch and operation of a total of approximately 45 to 60 BB satellites, and achieve Continuous SpaceMobile Service in all targeted geographical markets to meet our long term business goals with the launch and operation of a total of approximately 90 BB…
We anticipate launching and deploying additional satellites beyond the initial 90 satellites in order to enhance coverage and system capacity in response to incremental market demand.

We have recognized revenue from completion of performance obligations in agreements with the U.S. government either directly or indirectly through prime contractors utilizing the initial BB satellites and expect to continue to recognize revenue as and when we complete the remaining performance obligations under the agreements.

We have also generated revenue from the sale of gateway equipment, software and related services to MNOs and expect to continue to generate revenue as MNOs build out ground infrastructure for commercial readiness.
We plan to utilize the initial BB satellites to initiate intermittent coverage in targeted geographical markets, including in the United States.
We expect to continue to activate fixed cells, test the SpaceMobile Service automation, and integrate our network to MNOs’ core networks prior to rollout of the initial intermittent coverage.
Additionally, we rely on contractual agreements with MNOs to access some of the spectrum we will utilize to provide services.
We currently do not expect potential interruptions to our operations in Israel to have a material impact on the Company.
Our historical financial performance has been, and we expect our financial performance in the future to be, driven by our ability to execute on our strategy.

We began depreciating the BB6, BB8, BB9, and BB10 satellites as of September 1, 2026 over their expected remaining useful lives of approximately 84 months and the Block 1 BB satellites as of October 29, 2024 over their expected remaining useful lives of approximately 60 months.

If we are unable to achieve the supply chain diversifications, cost reductions, process improvements, and secure favorable future launch contracts, the average capital cost of the Block 2 BB satellites will be higher and such variations could be material.
We believe we can develop satellite configurations that target delivering service to certain attractive markets without the necessity of building a constellation which covers the entire globe.

We plan to raise additional capital through the issuance of equity, equity-linked or debt securities (secured or unsecured), secured or unsecured loans or other debt facilities, and credit from government or financial institutions or commercial partners.
There can be no assurance that additional funds will be available to us on favorable terms or at all.

In consideration for the license, we will pay Firefly $400.0 million in cash and an estimated 10 to 14 million in shares of our Class A Common Stock, a portion of which is subject to lock-up, as determined by a forward VWAP calculation.

The shares will be issued pursuant to an effective registration statement of the Company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission; however, 2.4 million shares will be freely tradable at closing, with the remaining shares subject to a lock-up that permits additional shares to be sold at six months, one year and three years post-closing.

As consideration for the Supply and Services Agreement, we will pay Firefly (1) a services fee of $250.0 million over a three-year period and (2) a hardware fee of $250.0 million for delivery of the engines for our first three rockets.
RAST is expected to be funded by the grant award and our investments in RAST through preferred shares subscriptions, as discussed below.
Such funds will be used to buy satellites, launch support services, and software licenses from us, and establish the infrastructure to deploy and manage the J-LEO Constellation.
We will subscribe for no coupon preferred shares to fund the remaining cost (above the grant award) for the deployment of the J-LEO Constellation.

The amount of our subscription is subject to numerous factors such as satellite materials and launch costs and our preliminary estimate is that the subscription will be approximately $1.4 billion over an approximately three year period.

The remaining capacity of the J-LEO Constellation will be used solely by us to provide services to our customers worldwide subject to regulatory approvals, with us sharing a pre-determined low single digit percentage of qualifying revenue with RAST.
The revenue earned by RAST is expected to be used, subject to shareholders deciding otherwise, to reinvest in expanding the constellation and buying additional satellites from us.
Under the Satellite Supply Agreement, we will supply satellites to RAST.

Under the Rakuten License Agreement, we will provide a non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-sublicensable license to RAST of our mission control and monitoring software to establish the Japan satellite operations center and the Japan payload operations center.

On January 5, 2025, AST LLC entered into a binding agreement (the “Strategic Collaboration Term Sheet”) with Ligado LLC under which we will receive long-term access to up to 45 MHz of lower mid-band spectrum in the United States and Canada for direct-to-device satellite applications.

The funds under the $520.0 million Backstop Commitment will be available to be drawn by Ligado only in the event the applicable regulatory approvals are not obtained in accordance with the definitive documents between us and Ligado, and is subject to the satisfaction of certain other limited conditions.
Upon conversion, we will pay or deliver, as the case may be, cash, shares of our Class A Common Stock or a combination of cash and shares of our Class A Common Stock, at our election.

We intend to use the remaining net proceeds to pursue an expanding universe of growth initiatives and secure additional access to orbit for our space-based cellular broadband network, including partnerships and/or acquisitions to further vertically integrate our business and mitigate risks associated with third-party launch providers.
